core_problem: A browser-based, bring-your-own-key AI website builder: a multi-provider tool-calling agent writes a React/TS/CSS project into a virtual filesystem, bundles it in the browser with esbuild-wasm, executes it in a hidden iframe to catch runtime errors, and deploys the result to Cloudflare Pages without any server-side code execution.
architecture: React 19 + Vite SPA; Supabase for auth/Postgres/Realtime; Vercel functions in api/ (deploy, provider-keys, admin, supabase-oauth) sharing api/_shared.ts (JWT check, rate limit, AES-256-GCM key encryption) and re-implemented as dev middleware shims in vite.config.ts. The product core is src/lib/agent.ts (3.8k lines): runOpenThornAgent() drives a tool loop (MAX_TOOL_TURNS=30) over 12 providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama) with per-call retry/backoff/Retry-After, a circuit breaker (3 failures, 30 s cooldown), mid-run provider failover (max 2), context compaction (estimateMessageTokens, KEEP_RECENT_TURNS=6, summary every 6 turns), and a LoopDetector that fingerprints only FAILING tool calls (3 repeats of an action or error -> loopBreakPrompt nudge). Tools (src/lib/agent-prompt.ts AGENT_TOOLS, alphabetically sorted for byte-identical cache prefixes): think, set_title, load_skill, list_files, read_file, search_files, write_file, edit_file, multi_edit, delete_file, set_schema, compile, done; selectToolsForRun() picks a core / small-refine / expanded tool set once per run. The system prompt is byte-identical across calls (dynamic state goes in <system-reminder> user messages) and skills (SKILL_BLOCKS: ui-ux-pro-max, frontend-design, react-best-practices, motion-dev-animations, performance, core-web-vitals, shadcn, karpathy-guidelines) are loaded on demand via load_skill. Write path: write_file runs agent-lint.normalizeWrittenCode (strip unused react imports, whitespace) and shouldRejectWholeFileRewrite() (refine mode, file >=160 lines, new >=65% of old size, preservedLineFraction >= 0.55 or small-refine prompt -> reject and demand multi_edit unless the prompt says rebuild/redesign). compile tool: preview-bundle.buildPreview() bundles the virtual FS via esbuild-wasm + virtualFsPlugin, with an import map that pins React 18.2 from esm.sh, a data-URL hash router replacing react-router-dom, and only packages in allowed-packages.ts (framer-motion, lucide-react, recharts, clsx, date-fns, nanoid, supabase-js; the same list is rendered into the prompt); then preview-runtime-check.runtimeSmokeTest() injects a capture script into the HTML, runs it in a sandboxed iframe (1.4 s settle, 8 s hard timeout) and reports uncaught errors, console.error, whether #root rendered, route 404s and NaN canvas draws; a passing compile sets runCtx.lastCompileOk and clears dirtySinceCompile. done tool: runDoneVerificationGate() rejects with a structured DONE_REJECTED error if (1) files changed since the last passing compile, (2) findOrphanedStylesheets() finds a .css with rules that nothing imports, (3) findDisallowedImageSources() finds remote images outside an allowlist of free hosts (unsplash/picsum/placehold.co), or (4) interactiveSmokeTest() (clicks interactive elements, checks DOM changed, no handler errors) fails; inconclusive checks never block. agent-memory.ts persists lessons.md (FIX/PATTERN/GOTCHA/TRIED/WORKS) and a CHANGELOG.md across sessions; pending error lessons are promoted only after a subsequent passing compile. set_schema declares Supabase tables (access: owner/public_read/authenticated) and api/_schema.ts generates RLS-enabled migrations. Templates (src/lib/templates.ts, 2.4k lines) are nine hand-written starter projects as file arrays. Visual click-to-edit swaps the jsx-dev-runtime for a shim that stamps data-oeid on host elements (preview-edit.ts / preview-inspect.ts).
core_innovation: A deterministic 'done' verification gate that refuses the model's completion claim unless the exact current files have passed an in-browser build, a runtime execution smoke test, an interactive smoke test, and cross-file lint checks (orphaned stylesheet, image licensing).
strengths: runDoneVerificationGate is exactly the 'gate before generator' posture: stale-compile, orphaned stylesheet, image-host licensing and interactive smoke test are all pure, reproducible checks that reject the model's 'done' with a structured, retryable error and a concrete suggestion.

compile = build AND execute: esbuild only transpiles, so the bundle is actually run in a sandboxed iframe with error/console/#root/route/canvas-NaN capture; 'build succeeded but crashes at runtime' is treated as failure.
allowed-packages.ts is a single dependency-free source of truth consumed by both the bundler's import map and the prompt; the model literally cannot import anything else.

Prompt-cache discipline: byte-identical system prompt, alphabetically sorted tool schemas, tool set chosen once per run, dynamic state only in <system-reminder> messages; skills loaded on demand by id.

Whole-file-rewrite guard (preservedLineFraction) and write-time lint hooks bind hygiene to the harness rather than the model's memory; LoopDetector counts only failing calls to avoid false positives on healthy edit/compile rhythms.
Robust provider layer: retry with Retry-After, circuit breaker, mid-run failover, malformed tool JSON returned to the model as structured errors, per-run token/cache telemetry.
Cross-session memory with a promotion rule (error lessons only become 'recovered lessons' after a passing compile) and a TRIED/FAILED changelog to avoid dead ends.
Good test coverage for the deterministic parts (agent-lint, preview-bundle, preview-edit/inspect, edit-fuzzy-match, virtualFsPlugin, schema-compiler).
weaknesses: It is a code generator (React + CSS in a virtual FS), the exact fragile paradigm we are avoiding; quality depends on the model writing good CSS, and the design 'skills' are aspirational prompting ('BOLD aesthetic direction', 'UNFORGETTABLE', 'NEVER use Inter') that the brief explicitly rejects.
No structured site model, no section library, no design-system tokens as data; 'design language' is whatever the skill prose induces. Output is not reviewable as a contract.
Image licensing gate is host-allowlist only (Unsplash/Picsum/placeholders), i.e. it steers toward generic stock, and there is no real-photo/art-direction layer at all.
In-browser esbuild-wasm preview pins React 18.2 from esm.sh and replaces react-router-dom with a hash router: the preview environment is not the deploy environment.
Single developer, 23 stars, no LICENSE file, package still named bloom, logs and a Remotion ad committed; the 3.8k-line agent.ts and 3k-line ProjectBuilderPage.tsx are hard to extract from.

Runtime checks are heuristic (1.4 s settle, click-everything smoke test) and 'inconclusive never blocks', so the gate can pass a page that is visually broken; there is no axe/Lighthouse/schema validation.
Sensitive product concerns for us: Adsterra ad banners, admin panel, blog CMS, community page: most of the repo is product surface unrelated to generation.
patterns_to_steal: Deterministic done-gate with structured retryable rejections (code, message, suggestion) -> our Launch QA gate: the agent's 'ship' call is refused unless the current SiteDefinition hash matches the last passing Playwright/axe/Lighthouse/placeholder run; rejection payload names the failing check and the fix.
Stale-compile tracking (dirtySinceCompile + lastCompileOk + cached last preview) -> Assembly/QA: hash the SiteDefinition and reuse the last QA report when unchanged; any mutation invalidates it.

Cross-file deterministic lints that pass the compiler but break the page (orphaned stylesheet, disallowed image hosts) -> Anti-slop tier 1 and Launch QA: unreferenced assets, images not from the FactRegistry/asset store, sections referencing missing facts.

Single-source allowlist consumed by both the runtime resolver and the model-visible catalogue (allowed-packages.ts) -> Eligibility/Creative Direction: the eligible design_system_ids, art_direction_ids and variants shown to the model must be the same objects the renderer accepts; generate the prompt catalogue from them.
Prompt-cache discipline (static system prompt, sorted tool schemas, per-run tool set, dynamic state in reminders) -> agent orchestration for every model call in the pipeline.
LoopDetector that fingerprints only failing actions and injects a nudge -> agent orchestration for the audit/fix loop.
Whole-file-rewrite guard (preservedLineFraction) -> visual editor / fix loop: reject a model 'fix' that rewrites most of a section when the prompt was a small refine; require a targeted patch.
Lessons promoted only after a passing verification -> Telemetry -> priors promotion: a prior only moves when a later gate confirms the fix.
patterns_to_avoid: Skill prompts like frontend-design.ts ('pick an extreme tone', 'never use Inter', 'unexpected layouts') -> aspirational prompting is rejected; taste must be encoded in authored design systems and section variants, not adjectives.
Generating React/CSS source as the artefact -> our artefact is SiteDefinition JSON rendered by Astro; the model never writes markup.
Stock-photo host allowlist as the image policy -> we need real owner photos with asset_constraints and art direction; stock URLs would fail our 'real photos' rule.
In-browser bundling with pinned esm.sh React and a hash-router shim -> preview must be the real Astro build, not an approximation.
Karpathy/ui-ux-pro-max style mega-prompts (hundreds of rules) -> rules that can be checked should be code (axe, regex, budgets), not prompt text.
reusable_patterns: DoneVerificationGate: the completion tool is refused unless the current artefact hash has passed all deterministic checks; rejection is structured and retryable.
BuildThenExecute: treat 'compiles' as insufficient; run the artefact in a sandbox and capture runtime/console/render signals.
SharedAllowlist: one dependency-free module defines what the model may reference and what the runtime will resolve.
StaticPromptDynamicReminder: keep system prompt and tool schemas byte-stable; move per-turn state into reminder messages.
FailingCallLoopDetector: fingerprint only errored tool calls and repeated error messages; nudge after N repeats.
PreservedLineFractionGuard: reject wholesale rewrites when most of the original survives verbatim.
VerifiedLessonPromotion: memory entries derived from errors are promoted only after a later passing check.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Ignore the product and the code-generation paradigm, but port the verification harness ideas into our QA gate and agent loop: a structured done/ship gate keyed to the artefact hash, build-then-execute smoke tests (our equivalent is the Astro build plus Playwright crawl), cross-file deterministic lints, the shared allowlist pattern for eligible ids, and the prompt-cache/loop-detection discipline. These are 100-300 line mechanisms each and map cleanly onto TypeScript. Explicitly do not port the skill prompts or the image-host policy.
